stem: In an animal study, the facial nerve is cut in one group and the optic nerve in another. After 3 months the facial nerves have regrown, but the optic nerves show no regrowth.
oneliner: Study: cut facial nerve regrows in 3 months + cut optic nerve does not → why?
ask: Which of the following best explains the difference?

options.A: Its ganglion cells are derived from neural crest, which cannot regenerate
options.B: Retinal vessels cannot grow into the cut nerve ends
options.C: Regrowing fibers are unable to cross the optic chiasm
options.D: Its axons are myelinated by oligodendrocytes, which block regrowth
options.E: Photoreceptors release signals that block axon regrowth

whyNot.A: Ganglion cells come from **neuroectoderm of the diencephalon**; neural crest gives the Schwann cells that **help** regrowth
whyNot.B: Cut axons regrow from their **own stump**; a vessel problem would not explain why the **facial nerve regrew** after the same injury
whyNot.C: The optic nerves show **no regrowth at all**, so crossing the chiasm is not the issue
whyNot.E: Photoreceptors are not the cells of the optic nerve; **ganglion cell axons** form it

answer: Optic nerve is CNS (diencephalon outgrowth); oligodendrocyte myelin inhibits regeneration
why: The optic nerve grows out of the **diencephalon**, so it is a **CNS tract** myelinated by **oligodendrocytes**, whose myelin **inhibits regrowth**. The facial nerve is PNS, myelinated by **Schwann cells** (neural crest), which support regeneration.

idea.rule: CNS axons are myelinated by oligodendrocytes and regenerate poorly; PNS axons use Schwann cells and regenerate.
also: Optic nerve and retina are CNS (diencephalon)
Oligodendrocyte: one cell myelinates many CNS axons
Schwann cell: one cell myelinates one PNS axon
Multiple sclerosis affects CNS myelin, Guillain-Barre PNS myelin
